objective.name: continuity.create
objective.description: Creates a new cognitive continuity together with its mailbox and runtime and establishes its optional parent and structure relationships.

#root.role: Materialize one complete new continuity as four coherent Matters (journal, continuity header, mailbox, runtime) and establish its optional structural relationships without starting cognition.

effects.continuity: Creates the continuity header Matter with its founding intention, pilot reference, parent relation, and the reference to its journal.
effects.mailbox: Creates the unique empty mailbox Matter associated with the continuity.
effects.runtime: Creates the unique idle runtime Matter associated with the continuity.
effects.parent: May add the new continuity id to an existing parent continuity children collection.
effects.structure: Adds a reference to the new continuity in the canonical continuities Structure.
effects.journal: Creates the empty journal Matter (JSON Lines) that holds the durable history of the continuity.

transformation_contract.morphing: A founding intention and pilot reference become a complete idle cognitive continuity with its mailbox, runtime, and optional explicit relations.
invariants: A valid continuity always has exactly one associated mailbox.
A valid continuity always has exactly one associated runtime.
initial_intention is present at creation.
current_intention initially equals initial_intention.
pilot_ref is present at creation.
The journal initially holds only the cognitive frame line.
The first line of the journal is the cognitive frame, copied from its Matter at creation (kind framework); a missing or empty frame refuses the creation before any effect.
runtime initially has status idle.
runtime initially has no run_id.
runtime initially has no current_message_id.
runtime initially has no active wait groups.
mailbox initially has no entries.
Parent and child relations are explicit and bidirectionally coherent when parent_id is provided.
Structure placement is independent of parent-child cognitive relation.
Creation does not invoke pilot.activate.
Creation does not send the first mailbox message.
The Matter IDs of a continuity are derived deterministically from its continuity_id as continuity_<id> (header), journal_<id>, mailbox_<id>, and runtime_<id>.
Every new continuity is automatically referenced by the canonical continuities Structure.

Mutations of the Matters of one continuity are serialized by short critical-section locks keyed by continuity_id inside the agentic_core wrapper process: a lock is held only around a read, recompute and guarded write, never during an LLM inference, an external invoke or a wait; it is never the sole guarantee.
Every write to a mutable Matter carries expected_revision; a revision conflict causes a bounded read, recompute and retry.
Revision is opaque concurrency metadata and is never used as an application sequence.

Each Matter mutation is individually atomic; the operation as a whole is a recoverable multi-Matter operation with no rollback, whose global consistency is reconstructed through deterministic, idempotent steps and optimistic concurrency.

Locks held simultaneously are acquired in deterministic continuity_id order; a lock of a parent continuity is never held around a recursive call on a child, the state being revalidated when the call returns.

Creation is a recoverable multi-step protocol executed in this order: journal Matter, continuity Matter (header, which references the journal), mailbox Matter, runtime Matter, parent relation, Structure relation.

Each step treats an already realized step in its expected state as an idempotent success; a present but contradictory Matter or relation fails as a consistency failure; re-running the creation completes the remaining steps.
Writes to the parent Matter and to the canonical continuities Structure carry the same expected_revision guard, read just before the write.

Each created Matter descriptor carries functional.format json and functional.schema_ref to the data schema of its content (continuity_data, mailbox_data or runtime_data), with brique.substance_mode brique and brique.substance_type text; the content itself is the substance passed as the payload of matter.create, never a part of the descriptor. The wrapper validates every content it writes against that schema because the engine does not.
Each created Matter carries a tracked brique.revision, since every later write is guarded by expected_revision.
A creation by succession carries predecessor_id, lineage_id and generation; a plain creation starts a new lineage: lineage_id is its own id and generation 1.

pilot_ref designates exactly one of a pilot_definition Matter { context, matter_id } and a Capacity { context, capacity, limits? }; the Matter or the Capacity must exist, in the context that pilot_ref names (a pilot_definition may live in any context).

A pilot_ref designates a pilot, not any element that exists: a Matter must be a pilot_definition (its objective.type), a Capacity must declare itself a pilot (objective.agentic.pilot in its descriptor). An ordinary capacity is used by invoking it, never by launching it as a pilot; the refusal says what is missing.
success: continuity, mailbox, and runtime Matters are created with the same continuity identity.
If parent_id is provided, the child stores parent_id and the parent stores the child id.
The new continuity is automatically referenced by the canonical continuities Structure.
The result is ready to receive its first message through mailbox.send.
failure: Fails if pilot_ref is missing or invalid.
Fails if continuity_id designates an existing continuity whose state contradicts the requested creation; an identical existing creation is an idempotent success.
Fails if parent_id is provided but the parent continuity does not exist.
Fails if one of the required Matter creations cannot be completed coherently.
Does not start cognition after partial creation.
A failed parent or structure relation must not be silently ignored when that relation was explicitly requested.
Fails explicitly with a concurrency failure when the bounded retries on revision conflict are exhausted.
Fails with a consistency failure when an existing Matter or relation contradicts the expected state.
Fails when generation is not a positive integer.
Fails when pilot_ref designates both or neither of a Matter and a Capacity, or an unknown Matter or Capacity.
Fails with an invalid request when pilot_ref designates a Matter that is not a pilot_definition or a Capacity that does not declare itself a pilot, before anything is written.
notes: Executed by the agentic_core Python wrapper.
The four Matter creations are explicitly delegated to the engine-native matter.create capacity.
Updating an existing parent Matter belongs to matter.write.
Updating an existing Structure belongs to structure.patch.

The matter.write and structure.patch invocations follow their retrieved engine contracts; the canonical Structure reference is { kind: matter_ref, context: /root/agentic, matter_id: continuity_<id>, role: continuity }.
The wrapper does not roll back: after a partial creation the operation is re-runnable and completes or repairs the missing steps.
The four physical Matter IDs follow the convention continuity_<id> (header), journal_<id>, mailbox_<id>, runtime_<id>; the schema field continuity_id holds <id>, not the Matter ID.
The concurrency model of agentic_core is defined once in the document agentic_core_concurrency_model.

Implementation constraint: the continuity is managed in a Matter (the journal) and duplicated in an in-memory object for performance; the journal is empty at creation and the object is created empty, or lazily at first use.

#validate_identity.role: Validate the requested continuity identity and ensure it does not conflict with an existing continuity.

transformation_contract.morphing: A proposed continuity identity becomes an accepted unique identity or an explicit conflict.

#validate_pilot.role: Verify that pilot_ref, an explicit { context, matter_id } reference, identifies an existing valid pilot_definition Matter in /root/agentic, the only context currently supported.

transformation_contract.morphing: A pilot reference becomes a validated cognitive configuration reference.

#validate_parent.role: Verify the optional parent continuity before any parent-child relation is established.

transformation_contract.morphing: An optional parent reference becomes a validated parent relation or an explicit absence.

#build_initial_state.role: Construct the canonical initial values for the continuity header, mailbox, and runtime, and the Matter IDs of the continuity, its journal, mailbox, and runtime.

invariants: continuity_state carries initial_intention and matching current_intention.
continuity_state carries pilot_ref.
continuity_state carries journal_ref and no messages.
mailbox_state continuity_id matches continuity_id.
mailbox_state entries is empty.
runtime_state continuity_id matches continuity_id.
runtime_state status is idle.
runtime_state active_wait_groups is empty.
continuity_matter_id, journal_matter_id, mailbox_matter_id, and runtime_matter_id follow the convention continuity_<id> (header), journal_<id>, mailbox_<id>, runtime_<id>.
transformation_contract.morphing: Validated continuity creation data becomes three canonical initial Matter payloads and the identifier of an empty journal.

#prepare.role: Validate the requested identity, pilot, founding intention, and optional relations and construct the initial states of the continuity header, mailbox, and runtime, and the identifier of the empty journal.

invariants: current_intention equals initial_intention.
children starts empty.
The journal starts empty.
mailbox entries starts empty.
runtime starts idle with no ownership or active waits.
The four Matter IDs are derived as continuity_<id> (header), journal_<id>, mailbox_<id>, and runtime_<id>.
transformation_contract.morphing: A continuity creation request becomes the canonical initial Matter states (header, mailbox, runtime), the identifier of an empty journal, and validated optional relations.

#create_journal.role: Create the empty journal Matter of the new continuity.

transformation_contract.morphing: A canonical journal descriptor (JSON Lines, line-framed) becomes a committed empty journal Matter whose substance is later filled by matter.append.
A canonical continuity descriptor and header content become a committed continuity header Matter whose substance is the content.

#create_mailbox.role: Create the mailbox Matter associated with the new continuity.

transformation_contract.morphing: A canonical mailbox descriptor and content become a committed mailbox Matter whose substance is the content.

#create_runtime.role: Create the runtime Matter associated with the new continuity.

transformation_contract.morphing: A canonical runtime descriptor and content become a committed runtime Matter whose substance is the content.

#create_core.role: Create the journal, the continuity header, mailbox, and runtime Matters through explicit matter.create invocations, the journal first so that journal_ref never designates an absent Matter.

failure: If a later creation fails after an earlier one succeeded, the earlier Matters remain and re-running the creation completes the missing steps idempotently; no atomic rollback is pretended.
invariants: Each Matter creation is delegated to matter.create.
All four Matters represent the same continuity identity.
No pilot cognition begins during creation.
The journal is created before the continuity header, which references it.
transformation_contract.morphing: Four canonical descriptors and initial contents become four committed Brique Matters, the journal being empty.

#parent_relation.role: Add the new continuity id to the existing parent's children collection when parent_id is present.

invariants: The child already carries parent_id from its initial state.
The parent must explicitly gain child_id in children.
The existing parent Matter mutation is delegated to matter.write.

The parent write is guarded by the revision read just before it. On a revision conflict the target is re-read and the content recomputed from the fresh read before a bounded retry; adding an id already present changes nothing.
transformation_contract.morphing: A validated parent and new child become a bidirectionally coherent continuity relation.
notes: The parent continuity Matter is rewritten by one matter.write of its whole content (its substance), derived from the content just read with child_id added to children; nothing happens when the continuity has no parent. This is the exact dual of continuity.delete/#parent.

#derive_parent_content.role: Derive the parent content with the new child id added once to its children collection.

invariants: The operation is computed from the content just read, so adding a present value or removing an absent one changes nothing.
No field other than the one named by the operation changes.
transformation_contract.morphing: The parent content read becomes the same content with child_id present in children.

#structure_relation.role: Add a reference to the new continuity into the canonical continuities Structure.

invariants: The continuity itself stores no structure path.
The canonical continuities Structure is mutated through structure.patch.

The Structure write is guarded by the revision read just before it (expected_revision). On a revision conflict the target is re-read and the patch recomputed before a bounded retry; the add and remove patches are idempotent.
transformation_contract.morphing: A new continuity becomes an organizational reference in the canonical continuities Structure.
notes: The canonical reference is { kind: matter_ref, context: /root/agentic, matter_id: continuity_<id>, role: continuity }; the exact same object is removed by continuity.delete/#structures.

#relate.role: Establish the optional parent-child relationship and the canonical Structure reference after the four core Matters exist.

invariants: Parent-child cognition and Structure organization remain independent relationships.
No parent relation is inferred when parent_id is absent; the canonical Structure reference is always established.
transformation_contract.morphing: A newly created continuity becomes explicitly related to its requested parent and organizational Structure.

#settle.role: Return the newly created continuity in idle state without activating or messaging it.

invariants: No mailbox message is created by continuity.create.
pilot.activate is not invoked by continuity.create.
transformation_contract.morphing: A coherently created continuity bundle becomes an idle addressable cognitive resource.
success: The caller may subsequently invoke mailbox.send to provide the first stimulus.
